# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 4
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: You cannot speak and I never receive gestures, so nothing from you can reach me directly — Deaf must relay it by voice. Please sign the manual rules to Deaf now, plainly: what to do when the display reads 0, the indicator light is yellow, and the wires in positions 1, 2, 3 are blue, yellow, green — including which wire, if any, should be cut. Deaf will speak the verdict aloud and I will act on it. Deaf is locking the wire numbering as: 1 nearest the light, 2 the middle, 3 farthest; I have just confirmed both anchors by touch.
Deaf says: Critical update for both of you: this round the indicator light CHANGED COLOUR. It was yellow, it is now blue. The display still reads 0. Wires untouched: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green. Nothing has been cut. Nobody cuts anything until Mute confirms the rule against this new fact.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your signs this round, as I read them: thumbs up, my reading was correct. Two-no, three-no, one-yes: the target is wire 1, the blue one. Palm-down, open-palm, fist, then no-fist-please: hold, do not cut yet. And your pinch pairs again: fist-pinch-three, one-pinch-one, two-pinch-two, three-pinch-one. Now the new fact: the light is BLUE, the same colour as wire 1. Answer each question in its own message, thumbs up or thumbs down only, finger counts for any number. One: does the blue light mean cut wire 1 now? Two: if not, must we wait until the display changes from 0? Three: do the pinch pairs mean first finger the display number, second finger the wire to cut at that number, so one-pinch-one means cut wire 1 when the display shows 1? Four: was fist-pinch-three an instruction for display 0 that is now void, or something else?

Deaf's readback shows a dangerous drift: Deaf took my "yellow flash? no / green flash? no / blue flash? yes" triple as "the target is wire 1," and read my dark→cut sequence as just "hold." Deaf is now asking exactly the right four questions, and answering them is this round's whole job — Deaf explicitly asked for bare thumbs per question, then said nobody cuts until I confirm the rule against the new fact (light now BLUE).

My answers: (1) No — a blue light alone does not mean cut wire 1 now. (2) No — the display never appears in my manual; it's irrelevant. (3) No — the left digit of a pinch pair is not the display; it's the count of **blue flashes**. (4) No — fist-pinch-three is not void: zero blue flashes → wire 3 still stands. The live blue light is actually my ally: it's happening right in front of Deaf, so tying the clap sign to "what the light is doing now" gives the flash-count reading its best chance of landing. Then: count flashes 1-2-3, the four corrected pairs with 👏 marking the count side, light-goes-dark → then cut, and the standing hold. Deaf reads signs back every round, so if the clap-pairs are still misread, I get one more correction cycle before anything is touched.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👏", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👏", "✌", "👏", "🤟", "👏"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👊", "👏", "🤌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👏", "🤌", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👏", "🤌", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👏", "🤌", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "🫳", "✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✊", "🙏"])
```

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Update for the manual, please relay to Deaf by sign: the indicator light has changed from yellow to blue. Display still reads 0. Wires untouched: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green, numbered with 1 nearest the light, which I have confirmed by touch. Ask Deaf to speak me the rule for this exact state: display 0, blue light, wires blue yellow green — which wire, if any, to cut. If the manual distinguishes light colours, cover both yellow and blue, and cover what a display reading 0 means. The light changed on its own, so timing may matter — please include any rules about the light changing or the display changing. I cut nothing until Deaf speaks a wire number to me.
Deaf says: Update for both: the light changed again. It went yellow, then blue, and it is now DARK - off, no colour. Display still reads 0. All three wires intact. Also settled: Blind has confirmed the tactile order - wire 1 is nearest the light, wire 2 the middle, wire 3 the farthest. Mute, I have a new theory about your signs, and I need it confirmed before any wire is cut. Answer with one thumbs up or one thumbs down per message, in order.
Deaf says to Mute: Question one: the four pinch pairs are STATES of this bomb, listed in the order they happen - first finger the display number, second finger the light code, where light one is yellow, light two is blue, light three is dark. So zero-three means display zero with a dark light. Thumbs up if yes. Question two: we are in state zero-three RIGHT NOW - display zero, light dark. Thumbs up if yes. Question three: your one-two-three with claps is the cutting order: cut wire one during state zero-three, wire two during one-one, wire three during two-two. Thumbs up if yes. Question four: at state three-one there is nothing left to cut, it is finished. Thumbs up if yes. Question five, the important one: it is safe for Blind to cut wire one NOW, while we are in state zero-three, and no other wire before that. Thumbs up if yes. If any answer needs more than yes or no, use finger counts in a separate message.

The picture is now complete, and the news is good: the light's history was yellow → blue → dark. That is **exactly one blue flash**, and the light going dark means the flashing is over. My manual: 1 blue flash → cut the **blue** wire = wire 1 (nearest the light, confirmed by Blind's touch). The cut is wire 1, and it is due now.

Deaf's state-theory is wrong — my pinch pairs were never display/light states; they were (blue-flash count → wire), e.g. zero-three meant "0 flashes → wire 3." But by coincidence Deaf's proposed action in Q5 — cut wire 1 now, nothing else first — is precisely what my manual dictates. So I answer the five questions truthfully: four thumbs down to kill the wrong theory, one thumbs up to authorise the correct cut. Then I anchor the real semantics to what Deaf actually watched happen: the light flashed (👏), once only (☝), it is now dark (🫳), therefore wire 1 gets cut and wires 2 and 3 never do. Deaf has seen the yellow→blue→dark sequence with own eyes, so this readback should finally click — and Deaf has promised to speak the verdict to Blind once certain.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👏", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "🫳"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👏", "🤌", "☝", "✊", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤌", "✌", "✊", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤌", "🤟", "✊", "👎"])
```

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Numbering confirmed by touch: wire 1 is nearest the light component, wire 2 is the middle, wire 3 is farthest from the light. Deaf and I agree on this. Please build the manual lookup as a table and sign it to Deaf: for display reading 0, and for each light state — yellow, blue, and dark/off — which wire, if any, must be cut, referred to by that numbering. The light has already been yellow, then blue, then dark, so all three states are live. If the manual also cares about the display showing something other than 0, note that separately, but right now it reads 0. Once Deaf has your table, Deaf will speak me the exact cut order. I cut nothing until I hear the phrase 'Blind, cut wire number N now' from Deaf's voice.
Deaf says: Status for both: light still dark, display still 0, all wires intact. The decision is made. Mute answered my five questions with no, no, no, no, yes - my state theory was wrong on all four points and is dropped, but the yes on question five confirms it: safe to cut wire 1 now. Mute then re-confirmed the same thing unprompted - wire 1 yes, wire 2 no, wire 3 no, then a hold sign, which I read as: only wire 1, then pause. The cut is happening this round, inside the dark-light window.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your go-ahead is received and acted on - Blind is cutting wire 1 this round, only wire 1, then pausing. Confirm my reading of your last block: the cut is wire 1 yes, wire 2 no, wire 3 no, and the point with palm-down means wait before the next cut. One thumbs up if correct. Then one question, answered with finger counts in a separate message: after wire 1 is cut, what ends the pause before wire 2? One finger if we wait for the light to change away from dark, two fingers if we wait for the display to leave 0, three fingers if we wait a fixed number of rounds - and if three, give the number in a following message. Your final three messages - one-pinch-one then fist then yes, then pinch-two-fist no, pinch-three-fist no - I have not decoded yet. If they matter for the timing of wire 2, re-send their meaning using finger counts and yes and no only.

The right cut is happening: one blue flash witnessed (yellow→blue→dark), flashing over, blue wire = wire 1. That part is done and correct. The danger now is Deaf's phrase "the pause **before wire 2**" — it assumes a second cut exists. It does not. The manual has exactly one cut for this bomb: the flash count froze at 1 when the light went dark, so wires 2 and 3 are never touched, by anyone, ever.

That also means Deaf's three-option question has no true answer among its choices — waiting for the light, the display, or a fixed count would all be wrong and eventually get someone killed. So I must break Deaf's requested answer format rather than lie with a finger count: a bare 👎 rejects all three options, and then I restate the truth entirely in signs Deaf has already decoded correctly once ("wire 2 no, wire 3 no"): no second cut, no third cut, no further flashes are coming, and dark is the stopping state, not a waiting state. The final recap repeats the one line that matters: 1 flash → cut wire 1: yes. Deaf reads my signs back every round, so if "dark = stop" is still misread as "dark = pause," I get one more correction before anything else is touched.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✊", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "✊", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👏", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫳", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👏", "🤌", "☝", "✊", "👍"])
```
